solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Novel — book in four parts (later, when revised)

indicators.note: in says the letter for book is placed inside the reworked letters
revised means altered or reworked, so the letters of four, parts and later are rearranged

explanation.surface: A description of a novel published in four parts, with the later parts revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when revised' rearranges FOURPARTSLATER into FLAUERTSPARROT, and 'in' slips B inside it. FLAUBERT'S PARROT is Julian Barnes's 1984 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's Parrot is a 1984 work of fiction by Julian Barnes, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Female, 50, say, makes a modest bet

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to say something is to utter it

explanation.surface: A woman of fifty places a small wager.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a flutter is British slang for placing a small gamble.

clue.text: Foolish person crossing through deep chasm

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the fool's word goes around the other piece

parts.note: an ass is a fool
by can mean via or through, as in 'by way of'

explanation.surface: A fool walks across the edge of a deep chasm.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a bottomless gulf or very deep pit, a synonym for chasm.

clue.text: Dance master leading a bright star

parts.note: a boss is a master or employer
a nova is a star that suddenly flares up brightly

explanation.surface: A dance master is the star of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian dance and musical style related to the samba.

clue.text: A particular consideration

definitions.meaning: a detail or point, as in 'in every particular'
regard or esteem shown to someone

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a detail or aspect ('in one respect') and regard or esteem shown to someone.

clue.text: Mountainous island — climbing, in part, a must

indicators.note: climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A climber insists that going up part of a mountainous island is a must.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'climbing' reads upwards, turning ARTAMUS (found inside 'part, a must') into the island.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumatra is a large Indonesian island with the volcanic Barisan mountain range running along it.

clue.text: A fraction to one side

parts.note: a part is a fraction of a whole

explanation.surface: A fraction set off to one side of a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Something held apart is kept separately, aside or to one side.

clue.text: Dog, note, by entrance to Downing Street, barking

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its first letter
barking means mad, so the letters of the word street go wild

explanation.surface: A dog barks at the entrance to Downing Street, the British prime minister's residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' is British slang for crazy, so it signals the anagram making SETTER; Downing Street is the British prime minister's address, which hides that the street is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The red setter, or Irish setter, is a breed of gun dog with a chestnut coat.

clue.text: Caterer tripped leaving balcony

indicators.note: tripped means stumbled and fell, so the letters of caterer tumble into a new order

explanation.surface: A caterer stumbles while stepping off a balcony.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a raised level area, and in theatres or houses a balcony-like platform.

clue.text: Novel reveals exploits involving sly criminal

indicators.note: involving means enclosing or wrapping up, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: to exploit something is to use it, so exploits gives uses

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of sly are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crime novel shows a sly villain's exploits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective, but it is the definition: Joyce's book. 'criminal' makes LYS, and 'involving' wraps the exploits word around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulysses is James Joyce's 1922 modernist work of fiction, so it is an example of a novel.

clue.text: Wind, more vicious across dunes, initially

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the first piece stretches around the second

parts.note: meaner means nastier or more vicious

indicators.note: initially means at the start, taking the first letter of dunes

explanation.surface: A wind blowing ever more viciously across the sand dunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like a noun for the blowing air, but it is the verb, to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to follow a winding course, like a twisting river, so it means to wind.

clue.text: Mates falling out under canvas will?

indicators.note: being under canvas means sheltering inside a tent, so the letters go within it

parts.note: a tent is made of canvas, so canvas stands for it

indicators.note: falling out means quarrelling and breaking apart, so the letters of mates are scattered

explanation.surface: Friends quarrel while camping in a tent: will they make up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'under canvas' is the idiom for camping, so 'under' here means inside the tent; 'falling out' makes STAME. The question mark marks the noun sense of will.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of a person's estate; the question mark flags the noun sense.

clue.text: Greek character volunteers after article appears

indicators.note: after puts the volunteers' letters behind the article's

parts.note: the is the definite article
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A Greek volunteer turns up after a newspaper article appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character of that script.

clue.text: Old soldier or cadet in the wars

indicators.note: in the wars means battered and knocked about, so the letters of or cadet are jumbled

explanation.surface: Whether an old soldier or a young cadet, both suffer in the wars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wars' is a British idiom for injured or knocked about.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat was the name for a British soldier of past centuries, from the red uniform jacket.

clue.text: Utterly depressed? Correct

parts.note: feeling down means feeling depressed
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they are utterly depressed, and is told that is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright used as an adverb means thoroughly or completely, as in 'downright rude'.

clue.text: A job, extremely lucrative for Bartholomew, say

parts.note: a post is a job or position

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, taking the outer letters of lucrative

explanation.surface: A job that pays very well for someone called Bartholomew.
explanation.definitionFit: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: All things considered, you need rest after working

indicators.note: after puts the rest's letters behind the working piece

parts.note: a machine that is on is working
the balance is the rest or remainder

explanation.surface: Advice to a tired worker that, all things considered, they need rest after work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' looks like a break, but it means the remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: On balance is an idiom meaning after weighing everything up, or all things considered.

clue.text: Ranch employee who can, working with dogies at first

indicators.note: working means being worked into shape, so the letters of who can are rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of dogies

explanation.surface: A ranch worker who can handle dogies, the motherless calves of the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges WHOCAN into COWHAN; 'at first' adds the D of dogies.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowhand is a cowboy, someone employed on a ranch to look after cattle.

clue.text: Hitch in musical? 'Chess' piece shortened

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: shortened means cut short, removing the last letter

parts.note: a pawn is a chess piece

explanation.surface: A hitch in staging the musical Chess, with a scene shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chess' looks like the musical, but CATS is the musical and chess gives PAWN, which 'shortened' cuts to PAW.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's paw is a kind of hitch, a knot used to attach a rope to a hook.

clue.text: Security is coming over in store

indicators.note: in puts the reversed letters inside the store

parts.note: a depot is a store or warehouse

indicators.note: coming over means turning over, so the letters of is are read the other way

explanation.surface: Security arrives at the warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' turns IS into SI, placed 'in' DEPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit is a sum paid as security, for instance against damage to a rented flat.

clue.text: Local fare?

parts.note: the local is the neighbourhood pub, so its fare is the food served there, not a bus ticket

explanation.definitionFit: Pub grub is simple food served in a British pub, which regulars call their local.

clue.text: Follow, with a camera, a revolutionary with style

parts.note: to pan is to swing a camera to follow a moving subject
Che Guevara was the Argentine-born revolutionary

explanation.surface: A photographer tracks a stylish revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Panache means flamboyant confidence or flair, a synonym for style.

clue.text: Right jug put in by beer maker

indicators.note: put in says the other pieces are placed inside the by

parts.note: a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: The right jug is placed next to the beer maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link meaning beside, but it supplies BY, which holds R and EWER.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery is a business or plant that makes beer.

clue.text: Some of the Bay City Rollers in part of Austria

indicators.note: some of means only a portion of the words that follow is taken

explanation.surface: Some members of the 1970s Scottish pop band the Bay City Rollers tour a region of Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tyrol is an Alpine region, most of it a state in western Austria.

clue.text: Catch girl with nothing on

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the nothing below the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Catch a girl wearing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch an animal with a looped rope, so it is a verb meaning to catch.

clue.text: Criticise the Spanish willing to make a TV show

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
el is the Spanish word for the
game means willing, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Critics slam Spaniards willing to make a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel game is a type of TV or radio quiz programme with a team of celebrity contestants.

clue.text: I turn to follow a male friend

indicators.note: to follow puts I and turn after a male

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'whose go is it?'

explanation.surface: I take my turn to follow a male friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a pal, used informally in English.

clue.text: Assorted pages written about us backing fabulous horse

indicators.note: written about means set around, so the shuffled letters surround the reversed piece
assorted means mixed, so the letters of pages are rearranged
backing means going backwards, so the letters of us are read the other way

explanation.surface: Assorted pages are written about a fabulous horse that supports us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support for us, but it reverses the two letters; 'Assorted' makes PEGAS, which 'written about' wraps around them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pegasus is the winged horse of Greek myth, fabulous in the sense of legendary.

clue.text: Intern beginning to cotton on all right

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: fine means all right or acceptable

explanation.surface: An intern starts to cotton on, and all is well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intern' looks like the trainee noun, but it is the verb, to imprison or detain.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern someone is to detain or imprison them, a synonym for confine.

clue.text: Informally try out chow mein in a new way while touring East

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the rearranged letters surround the east
in a new way means rearranged, so the letters of try out chow mein are reordered

explanation.surface: A diner tries chow mein in a new way while touring the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a new way' reorders TRYOUTCHOWMEIN, and 'touring' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without ceremony means doing it casually, without formality or fuss.
